editionData.title: German nationalists’ big win sounds alarm for mainstream politicians in Europe; They formed to fight Haiti’s gangs. Now they’re...
editionData.description: Global headlines: German nationalists’ big win sounds alarm for mainstream politicians in Europe (“This has shaken us,” Chancellor Friedrich Merz said after Ulrich Siegmund led his Alternative for Germany party to victory in Saxony-Anhalt); They formed to fight Haiti’s gangs. Now they’re an obstacle to peace. (As a U.S.-backed, U.N.-authorized force attempts to restore security, “self-defense brigades” pose a unique challenge); and Nationalist AfD wins key regional election in Germany but falls short of majority (Alternative for Germany, labeled “extremist” by German authorities, polled first in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt but still might not control the government). Markets leaned lower, with 6 of 7 tracked indexes down; Nikkei 225 down 1.70% was the largest move. Benchmarks tracked: S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, Euronext 100 Index, and Public Joint-Stock Company Moscow Exchange MICEX-RTS plus 3 more indexes. Hacker News: Mistral raises €3B to make sovereign, open-weight AI the technology frontier (Mistral today announced that it has raised €3 billion in a Series D funding round at a post-money valuation of more than €21 billion); Navier-Stokes – Tristan Buckmaster [pdf] (cims.nyu.edu: Navier-Stokes – Tristan Buckmaster [pdf]); and We have a year to fix security everywhere (consumer-grade hardware can run an LLM that hacks the planet. we can stop it, but we don't have much time). hackerNews.title: How well do agents use test/verification techniques?
hackerNews.summary: We previously noted that, while it's easier than ever to hit a particular quality bar by having coding agents use effective test techniques, software quality seems to be getting worse , indicating that whatever defaults developers are using may not work very well. Here, we test if simple instructions to agents to use particular techniques or libraries improve implementation correctness, as a kind of test to see how effective agents are when guided by someone with no expertise in testing who's maybe heard that you should apply certain techniques or use certain libraries.
